column1: # The PC port's own menu strings, and the one place they are written.
# Bloodborne's option screens own one thousand-id block each: 110000 System,
# 111000 Environment, 112000 Brightness, 113000 Controls, 114000 Network,
# 115000 Language. Inside a block, N is a row and N+20 is the screen title -
# 110000..110005 are the System list's rows and 110020 is the word "System".
# The port takes the next free blocks - 116000 PC Settings, 117000 PC
# Graphics, 118000 PC Controls, 119000 Key Bindings, 120000 PC Effects, 121000
# PC Camera, 122000 the title menu's Quit to Desktop, 123000 Steam Deck (shown on a
# Deck only), 124000 PC Enhancements, 125000 PC Colour - and 110006..110014 for the System rows
# that open them, 110015 the System list's Quit to Desktop. All are unused in the shipped menu.msgbnd. (Motion blur,
# depth of field and chromatic aberration moved to PC Effects with their
# bb-engine-assets builds this file in and writes these into each language's
# menu.msgbnd.dcx at start (tools/engine/menu_assets.cpp); the ids are what
# gpu/shim/engine/option_menu.cpp and option_keys.cpp ask the message
# repository for, so the text lives here and nowhere else.
# Ids 920000..929999 are dialog text instead (group 78, the generic yes/no
# dialog's, and 204, the option screens' questions: Quit to Desktop asks
# 920001); the help column is unused.
# Ids 14000332..14000399 are event text (group 30): the talk menus' entries and
# the messages their scripts show - the Altar of Despair's rebirth
# (tools/engine/rebirth_script.h); the help column is unused.
# A "\n" in the text is a line break.
# Optional columns 4 and 5: Simplified Chinese text and help for msg/zhocn.
# Other language bundles retain the English columns. Empty translations fall back to English.
